## Question 1

Here is an example of some text, including this lovely plot: 

```{python}
#| label: plot_1
#| message: false
from plotnine import *
from plotnine.data import txhousing
from mizani.formatters import currency_format

# Filter data
cities = ["Houston", "Dallas", "Austin"]
df = txhousing[txhousing["city"].isin(cities)]

# Plot
(
    ggplot(df, aes(x="date", y="median", color="city"))
    + geom_point()
    + geom_line()
    + theme_bw()
    + xlab("Sale Date")
    + ylab("Median Home Price")
    + scale_y_continuous(labels=currency_format(prefix="$"))
    + scale_color_brewer(type="qual", palette="Dark2", name="City")
    + theme(legend_position="bottom")
    + ggtitle("TX Home Price Trends")
)
```

In this figure, we see that things are getting more expensive and that
Austin is generally more expensive than America's Greatest City, Houston.
